questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of National Income?

options.text: It is always expressed with reference to the financial year.
It is included only in intermediate goods.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is included only in intermediate goods.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• 
 The following are the main **characteristics **of national income:

 
 
• 
 **Macroeconomic concepts **include national income.
 
 
• 
 Taking into account the **monetary value **of goods and services is national income.
 
 
• 
 An **extended period **of **time **is used to **measure **national income.
 
 
• 
 Considerations for national income include the net **total values **of products and services.
 
 
• 
 National income solely takes into account the value of final items to prevent **double counting**.
 
 
 
 
• 
 When calculating national income, the value of **intermediate items **is not taken into account.
 
 
• 
 **Net factor income **from **abroad **is **included **in national income (NFIA).
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• In the simplest terms, national income refers to a **country's riches.**
 
• The value of the commodities and services generated in an economy serves as a gauge of its **prosperity**.
 
• It represents the overall **monetary **worth of the commodities and services that a country produces in the course of a **fiscal year**.
 
• **Rent, wages, profits, **and **interests** are a few examples of payments that can be paid to different kinds of resources.
 
• The idea of national income is under the ambit of **macroeconomics**.

questions.question: Vernacular press Act was enacted in which year?

The correct answer is __**1878.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Vernacular press act 1878**__

 __
 
• **​**__British India passed the Vernacular Press Act (1878) to restrict press freedom and discourage criticism of British policy, notably the opposition that had risen since the commencement of the Second Anglo-Afghan War (1878–80).
 
• The Act was submitted by Lytton, the Viceroy of India at the time, and on March 14, 1878, the Viceroy's Council unanimously approved it. In order to "better control" the vernacular press and effectively penalise and prohibit "seditious literature" in "publications in oriental languages," the Vernacular Press Act (VPA) was passed.
 
• As a result, the British had nothing but hatred for the (non-English speaking) Indian press.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The** Bengal Gazette** was the first newspaper to be printed in India. **James Hickey**, the editor of this publication, was a vocal opponent of the East India Company. The newspaper was shut down as a result within two years of starting to publish.
 
• The Bengal Gazette served as the model for a number of Indian newspapers that are presently printed in all major languages. **These journals carried editorials that were anti-colonial and attacked the East India Company's haughtiness.**
 
• The existence of such columns was crucial in educating the rapidly emerging educated Indian class about the brutal colonial authority that had been imposed upon India by a force that professed to support democracy.
 
• **The East India Company, which wished to uphold its hegemony in India despite all obstacles, was harmed by this. **Especially when the Second Anglo-Afghan War began in 1878, newspapers like Amrita Bazar Patrika and others were vociferous in their condemnation of the British in India.
 
• **Viceroy Lord Lytton, therefore,** created the Vernacular Press Act in 1878 to regulate seditious reports in vernacular newspapers published in India in an effort to stop this.

 Due to the agitation, it produced among the Indians, Lord Ripon abolished the Vernacular Press Act in 1881.

Conducting materials allows easy charge transfer because of the free movement of electrons through them.

 __

Since there is no electric field inside a conductor, electrons can move around freely.

 
 
• 
 
Inside a conductor, the charge density is zero.

 
 
• 
 
Free charges are only present on the conductor's surface.

 
 
• 
 
A conductor's points are all at the same potential.

 
 
• 
 
Many metals are effective electrical conductors. This is the rationale behind the use of metals in electrical appliance parts. Insulators are the plastic casings that shield electrical conductors. We won't experience an electric shock thanks to it.

• Omit all inverted commas or quotation marks.

• If it is in the **simple present tense (is)**, change it into the **simple past tense (was).**

• **Indirect:** The girl said that she liked singing.
